newsitem.title: USA: Calif. Microwave to restructure operations.
newsitem.headline: Calif. Microwave to restructure operations.

text.p: California Microwave Inc on Wednesday said it will restructure operations, cutting the staff of one of its business units by 20 percent and closing facilities in California and Illinois in its third quarter ending March 31.
In a written statement, the company said it will take an $8.0 million charge to account for the moves.

California Microwave, a supplier of satellite earth station and microwave radio infrastructure, said it will re-focus its two primary business divisions, Microwave Network Systems and Satellite Transmission systems.
The staff cuts will come from the Microwave Network unit, which will now focus on markets for personal communications services equipment and cellular communications equipment.
The majority of the $8.0 million charge will cover product warranty reserves at Microwave Network, the company said.
The Satellite Transmission division will focus on systems integration and network configuration. Its satellite earth station products will be transferred to another company division called EFData.

"The actions being taken are intended to restore overall profitability to the (two) operations by refocusing on core competencies, narrowing product lines and reducing costs," California Microwave said.
Earlier, the company reported a net loss of $1.57 a share for the second quarter ended December 31, including an initial $39 million charge for its restructuring plans.
Company officials were not immediately available for further comment.
In December, Chief Executive Officer Philip Otto resigned from the company and in January Chief Financial Officer Dennis Raney decided to leave the company at February's end.

The company has formed an executive committee headed by Chairman David Leeson to lead the company during its restructuring. George Spillane, currently vice president and secretary will assume Raney's duties when he departs.
